49918-the-land-of-promise-a-comedy-in-fo.title: A Comedy In Four Acts
49918-the-land-of-promise-a-comedy-in-fo.creator: W. S. Maugham
49918-the-land-of-promise-a-comedy-in-fo.description: A book by W. S. Maugham. The wall-paper has a  pattern of enormous chrysanthemums, and on the walls are a large  number of old-fashioned watercolours in gilt frames. There is one  door, which leads into the hall; and a French window opens on to  the garden. The window is decorated with white lace curtains. It is  four o’clock in the afternoon.

arxiv-2112-03153.title: On Discrete Approximations to Infinite Horizon Differential Games Thanks: This research has been partially supported by projects PID2022-136550NB-I00 funded by MICIU/AEI and FEDER (EU) (Javier de Frutos and Julia Novo) and TED2021-130390B-I00 funded by MICIU/AEI/10.13039/501100011033 and by European
arxiv-2112-03153.creator: Javier de Frutos, Victor Gatón, Julia Novo
arxiv-2112-03153.description: Abstract In this paper we study a discrete-time semidiscretization and a fully discretization (discrete-time, discrete-state) of an infinite time horizon noncooperative N N -player differential game. We prove that as either the discretization time step or both time step and mesh size parameters approach zero the discrete value function approximates the value function of the differential game.

arxiv-2201-12624.title: Reeb complexes and topological persistence
arxiv-2201-12624.creator: Melvin Vaupel, Erik Hermansen, Paul Trygsland
arxiv-2201-12624.description: Abstract We introduce Reeb complexes in order to capture how generators of homology flow along sections of a real valued continuous function. This intuition suggests a close relation of Reeb complexes to established methods in topological data analysis such as levelset zigzags and persistent homology.

arxiv-2311-03075.title: SoK: Memorisation in Machine Learning
arxiv-2311-03075.creator: Dmitrii Usynin 1,2 , Moritz Knolle 2,3 , Georgios Kaissis 1,2,3
arxiv-2311-03075.description: Abstract Quantifying the impact of individual data samples on machine learning models is an open research problem. This is particularly relevant when complex and high-dimensional relationships have to be learned from a limited sample of the data generating distribution, such as in deep learning.

arxiv-2311-07996.title: How Well Do Text Embedding Models Understand Syntax?
arxiv-2311-07996.creator: Yan Zhang, Zhaopeng Feng, Zhiyang Teng, Zuozhu Liu, Haizhou Li
arxiv-2311-07996.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yan Zhang, Zhaopeng Feng, Zhiyang Teng, Zuozhu Liu, Haizhou Li. Text embedding models have significantly contributed to advancements in natural language processing by adeptly capturing semantic properties of textual data. However, the ability of these models to generalize across a wide range of syntactic contexts remains under-explored.

arxiv-2412-12824.title: Enhancement of non-Gaussianity and nonclassicality of pair coherent states with postselected von Neumann measurement
arxiv-2412-12824.creator: Yi-Fang Ren 1 § , Janarbek Yuanbek 1 §, Yusuf Turek 1
arxiv-2412-12824.description: Abstract We investigate the effects of postselected von Neumann measurements on the nonclassical properties of pair coherent states (PCS). We calculated key quantum characteristics, such as squeezing, photon statistics, entanglement between the two PCS modes, and teleportation fidelity. Our results demonstrate that postselected von Neumann measurements enhance both the non-Gaussianity and nonclassicality of PCS.

arxiv-2507-21397.title: Enabling Pareto-Stationarity Exploration in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning: A Multi-Objective Weighted-Chebyshev Actor-Critic Approach
arxiv-2507-21397.creator: Fnu Hairi, Jiao Yang, Tianchen Zhou, Haibo Yang, Chaosheng Dong, Fan Yang, Michinari Momma, Yan Gao, Jia Liu
arxiv-2507-21397.description: Abstract In many multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) applications, being able to systematically explore the Pareto-stationary solutions under multiple non-convex reward objectives with theoretical finite-time sample complexity guarantee is an important and yet under-explored problem. This motivates us to take the first step and fill the important gap in MORL.

pmc-10698911.title: GATA6-AS1 suppresses epithelial–mesenchymal transition of pancreatic cancer under hypoxia through regulating SNAI1 mRNA stability
pmc-10698911.creator: Yunhui Zhou, Xinyi Zhou, Qiwen Ben, Ningning Liu, Jiahui Wang, Yongpeng Zhai, Yichen Bao, Lin Zhou
pmc-10698911.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a hypoxic microenvironment, a high rate of heterogeneity as well as a high likelihood of recurrence. Mounting evidence has affirmed that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) participate in the carcinogenesis of PDAC cells. In this study, we revealed significantly decreased expression of GATA6-AS1 in PDAC based on the GEO dataset and our cohorts, and showed that low GATA6-AS1 expression was linked to unfavorable clinicopathologic characteristics as well as a poor prognosis.

pmc-11328774.title: Percutaneous Treatment of a Left Ventricular Pseudoaneurysm Post-Aortic Valve Replacement
pmc-11328774.creator: Arpanjeet Kaur, Arber Kodra, Shankar Thampi, Ythan Goldberg, Chad Kliger
pmc-11328774.description: Left ventricular outflow tract pseudoaneurysm is rare but serious complication after aortic valve replacement and may occur secondarily to endocarditis, suture dehiscence, or morphologic changes at the aortic annulus. We present a case of successful percutaneous closure of a left ventricular outflow tract pseudoaneurysm using various cardiovascular imaging modalities.

pmc-11517046.title: Burden of disease due to ambient particulate matter pollution in Germany from 2010 to 2021
pmc-11517046.creator: D Plass, S Kienzler, D Wintermeyer
pmc-11517046.description: BackgroundWorldwide, according to the global burden of disease (GBD) study, around 118 million disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) were attributable to ambient particulate matter (PM2.5) in 2019. Further, 97% of Europe’s urban population are exposed to annual average levels of PM2.5 above the World Health Organization’s guideline value of 5 µg/m³. In Germany, considerable efforts have been made to reduce PM2.

pmc-11535990.title: Can yStage Ⅰ/Ⅱ rectal cancer patients be treated in the same way as stage Ⅰ/Ⅱ patients?
pmc-11535990.creator: Shumpei Mukai, Naruhiko Sawada, Yusuke Takehara, Kenta Nakahara, Yuta Enami, Fumio Ishida, Shin-ei Kudo
pmc-11535990.description: BackgroundNeoadjuvant therapy (NAT) before radical surgery are effective treatments for locally advanced rectal cancer. However, the treatment strategy after NAT and surgery is still unclear. It is difficult to accurately evaluate the stage before NAT, as some cases are downstaged by NAT.

pmc-11675014.title: Deconstructing the Mapper algorithm to extract richer topological and temporal features from functional neuroimaging data
pmc-11675014.creator: Daniel Haşegan, Caleb Geniesse, Samir Chowdhury, Manish Saggar
pmc-11675014.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Capturing and tracking large-scale brain activity dynamics holds the potential to deepen our understanding of cognition. Previously, tools from topological data analysis, especially Mapper, have been successfully used to mine brain activity dynamics at the highest spatiotemporal resolutions. Even though it is a relatively established tool within the field of topological data analysis, Mapper results are highly impacted by parameter selection.

pmc-13238587.title: Association between thyroid dysfunction and cognitive impairment in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross‐sectional study
pmc-13238587.creator: Mengmeng Zheng, Xing Zhong, Ping Zhang
pmc-13238587.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the association between thyroid dysfunction and cognitive impairment in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).MethodsIn this cross‐sectional study, 486 adult T2DM patients between January 2022 and January 2024 were enrolled. General clinical data and laboratory parameters [glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), thyroid‐stimulating hormone (TSH), free thyroxine (FT4)] were collected.

pmc-13374258.title: Continuous serratus–intercostal plane block versus intercostal cryoanalgesia for postoperative pain after minimally invasive cardiac surgery: a prospective comparative observational study
pmc-13374258.creator: Susana González-Suárez, Remedios Ríos-Barrera, Patricia Bascuñana Fornells, Berta Caralt Ramisa, Carlota M Vigil-Escalera, Cherif M Traore Kone, Isuru M Dammala Liyanage, Martha Magaly Paguay Fernández, Rafael Rodríguez-Lecoq
pmc-13374258.description: BackgroundMinimally invasive cardiac surgery via minithoracotomy is associated with postoperative pain. Continuous BRILMA (block of the lateral branches of the intercostal nerves in the mid-axillary line) and intercostal cryoanalgesia are opioid-sparing techniques, but comparative evidence in this setting is limited.

pmc-13637205.title: Establishing an efficacy hierarchy for breakthrough cancer pain management: a network meta-analysis of rapid-onset fentanyl formulations and morphine
pmc-13637205.creator: Po-Hung Tsao, Cho-Hao Lee, Jia-Hong Chen, Ching-Liang Ho, Hong-Jie Jhou, Po-Huang Chen
pmc-13637205.description: BackgroundBreakthrough cancer pain (BTP) is a common and debilitating condition affecting most patients with advanced malignancy. While multiple rapid-onset opioid formulations are available, a lack of comprehensive comparative evidence has hindered evidence-based treatment selection. We conducted a network meta-analysis (NMA) to evaluate the relative efficacy of all available formulations and characterize their temporal analgesic profiles for BTP management.
